question: In India, in relation to Census, what is the full form of NPR?
solution:
The correct answer is __**National Population Register.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **NPR stands for National Population Register.**
 
• It is a **database** maintained by the Government of India containing demographic and biometric details of **every citizen of the country.**
 
• The data collected through** NPR is used for various government schemes **and programs such as the issuance of Aadhaar cards, voter ID cards, and passports.
 
• NPR is updated periodically to ensure the accuracy of data and to include new citizens who have turned **18 years of age.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The NPR is a record of all the **usual residents of the country**.
 
• It is mandatory for every usual resident of India to register in the NPR.
 
• The NPR includes both Indian citizens and foreign citizens.
 
• The primary objective of the NPR is to create a comprehensive database of every usual resident in the country.
 
• **The NPR is prepared at various levels, including local (village/sub-town), sub-district, district, state, and national levels. This is done under the provisions of the Citizenship Act 1955 and the Citizenship (Registration of Citizens and Issue of National Identity Cards) Rules, 2003.**
 
• The data for the National Population Register was first collected in 2010 by the Government of India. The exercise is repeated every 10 years.
 
• The aim is to create a comprehensive identity database of every usual resident in the country. The database would contain both demographic and biometric details.
 
• The government ha**s clarified that no documents will be required for NPR **as a self-declaration will suffice for data entry in the population register.
